sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The soldier is of medium size, with a long, narrow, red-brown head, a long rostrum and long-segmented antennae, and a dark thorax and abdomen; the head is widest at about the posterior 1/3, narrowing abruptly towards the base of the rostrum, the rostrum slightly longer than 2/3 of the total head length, and the side of the head strongly concave in lateral view; the mandibles have well-developed pointed teeth. It is closest to E. tumuli and can be distinguished by the contracted and narrower head, the different lateral profile and the longer antennal segments. The alate is not recorded in the original.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text:
Large form: of medium size, with a long, narrow, red-brown head, a long rostrum and long-segmented antennae, and a dark thorax and abdomen. The hairs on the head, thorax and abdomen are few but rather long, together with many microtrichia. The posterior part of the head is chestnut, gradually becoming very dark brown anteriorly; the base of the rostrum is almost black and the apex red; antennal segment 1 is the same colour as the apex of the rostrum, the remaining segments dark brown; the thorax and abdomen are dark brown, the femora slightly paler. The head is widest at about the posterior 1/3 and narrows abruptly towards the base of the rostrum, which is slightly contracted there; the rostrum is slightly longer than 2/3 of the total head length; in lateral view the head is strongly concave at the middle of the capsule and from there almost straight nearly to the apex of the rostrum (in most individuals of one series the rostrum is bent downwards). Antennae usually 14-segmented (a few individuals 13-segmented, segments 3 and 4 completely or almost completely fused); segment 3 the shortest of all, slightly shorter than segment 2; segment 4 long, almost as long as segment 1; segment 5 shorter than segments 4 and 6; segments 6—13 long and narrow; segment 14 about as long as segment 2, elongate oval. Mandibles with well-developed pointed teeth. Small form: differing only in size and colour (slightly paler).
Measurements: large form body length 4.25 mm, head length (to apex of rostrum) 1.70—1.82 mm, head width 0.85—0.88 mm, pronotum width 0.52 mm; small form body length 3.25 mm, head length (to apex of rostrum) 1.42—1.53 mm, head width 0.68 mm, pronotum width 0.35 mm.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text:
Posterior part of the head chestnut (slightly darker than in the soldier), gradually becoming dark brown anteriorly; the base of the antennae brown, becoming yellow towards the apex; the postclypeus distinctly paler than the antennae; the thorax and abdominal tergites brown. Antennae 14- or 15-segmented (the original OCR reads "Ik or 15"), with segmentation varying as in the soldier. The cranial suture is very distinct. The thorax and the base of abdominal tergite 1 have a pale median line. The postclypeus is about half as long as wide.
Measurements: body length 4.75—6.00 mm; head length (to apex of labrum) 1.76 mm; head length (to clypeofrontal suture) 0.95—1.02 mm; head width 1.32—1.37 mm; pronotum width 0.57 mm.

note: Rewritten from the English species-level description in Hill (1942); the original gives it as Eutermes peracutus (the heading line was OCRed as 'peraoutus' and a figure caption as 'peraoutue'). The alate is recorded as 'Not known' in the original, so that section is not included. The antennal segment count of the worker was OCRed in the original as 'Ik or 15' and is read from the context as 14 or 15 segments. Distribution, Biology and Affinities are not translated into the morphological sections; the main points of Affinities have been compressed into Diagnostic characters. OCR misreadings: 'Pig.'='Fig.', 'lahrum'='labrum', 'anternae'='antennae', 'postciypeus'='postclypeus', 'Chicllow's Well' is a place name.
